block.goal: GET /users latency: author aggregation moved out of the 1.58G-RSS daemon

block_selection_reason: Resume block from the last tick event (duckbrain-foreman-2026-11-15-12-41-40) was OPS-014, which is now complete with no ready rows, so resume did not apply. block_drive.py --top 10 ranks PERF-015 first (1 pending, 9/10 done, P1) - the nearly-complete block rule selects it: finishing it removes a standing claim. PERF-015 is a singleton-wrapped block (the other 9 PERF rows are complete), so no wave can be composed from it; combined with slots=1 (see box_sizing) this tick is the serial path by both criteria.

box_sizing.slots_formula: max(1, min(6, nproc - ceil(loadavg))) = max(1, min(6, 16 - 21)) = 1
box_sizing.why: Host load 20.81 on 16 cores leaves < 2 slots, and the selected block is a singleton anyway; WAVE_BUDGET=8 is a ceiling, not a target. Serial with one worker, per the loaded-box rule - not an idle tick.

workers.title: GET /users runs the per-namespace author aggregation in a fork-light child process
workers.ownership: worker implements + tests + pushes wt/PERF-015; foreman judges, merges, rebuilds dist, restarts duckbrain-http.service, and runs the live acceptance

exclusions.why: owner ruling - a written decision, not buildable work; never dispatch a worker for it
not in the selected block; one block per tick
separate blocks with pending rows; not adjacent to PERF-015's acceptance target

control_capture.arm: live GET /users on the pre-change daemon, captured immediately before the change
control_capture.purpose: the row's corrected acceptance is set-equality against a same-store control captured BEFORE the change; this is that control

post_merge_acceptance: rebuild dist (npm run build:cli) in the canonical checkout
author SET equals control-summary authors_sha256 (order-insensitive), count reported honestly

git log --all child census during the request reported honestly (a fork-light helper still forks 338 times; the criterion's <= ~10 bound was a proxy for 'not inline' and is superseded by the child-process proof)
